name: Dotyali
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs are sociolinguistic surveys (Eichentopf 2014; Sapkota 2013) and a deixis paper; no phonology/grammar with a stress statement located

sources.citation: Bist, Nar Bahadur & Nirajan Bohara. 2026. An Action Research Study on the Pronunciation Challenges Faced by Doteli Students. International Research Journal of MMC 7(3): 28-37. doi:10.3126/irjmmc.v7i3.97068
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Generic remarks on L1 rhythm/stress influence on English (citing Wenk 1985 etc.); nothing specific about Doteli stress.

sources.citation: Thapa, Tej Bahadur. 2021. Place and Time Deixis in Doteli Language. MA thesis, Department of English Education, Tribhuvan University, Kirtipur. xiv+53 pp. https://elibrary.tucl.edu.np/handle/20.500.14540/10092
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Deixis only; the words 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' do not occur in a linguistic sense (a full-text search for stress/accent the full text).

sources.citation: Bist, Nar Bahadur. 2026. Improving English Pronunciation Among Doteli-Speaking Students. The EFFORTS, Journal of Education and Research 7(1): 130-149. doi:10.3126/ejer.v7i1.96785
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pedagogical action research; says only that 'Doteli-speaking learners have difficulty in producing several English consonants, vowels, consonant clusters, stress patterns and final consonants' (p. 132); no description of Doteli stress itself.
Vowel and consonant inventories only; no statement on stress, tone or accent; cites only Ethnologue, the Language Commission report, the constitution, Eichentopf 2014 and ISO 639-3.

sources.citation: Bhatt, Hari Sharan. 2023. Digital Implementation of Doteli Dictionary: A Tri-Lingual Dictionary for Doteli Language. Scholars' Journal 6: 33-48. doi:10.3126/scholars.v6i1.69993
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Software paper; useful only for its reference to Joshi, B. et al. 2022, Dotyali multilingual dictionary (Mahakali Sahitya Sangam). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Singh, Karishma. 2023. Grammatical Category of Nepali and Doteli Language. Academia Research Journal 2(1). doi:10.3126/academia.v2i1.52352
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nepali-language comparison of gender, number, person, tense, aspect, mood, voice, case; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: जोशी, धनकुमारी (Joshi, Dhankumari). 2018 (VS 2074). डोटेली भाषिकामा प्रचलित क्रियापदको अध्ययन [Study of the verbs current in the Doteli dialect]. MA thesis, Central Department of Nepali, Tribhuvan University. https://elibrary.tucl.edu.np/handle/20.500.14540/20182
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Verb morphology only (finite/non-finite verbs, tense, aspect); a short 'Doteli dialect' introduction (3.4); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: बोगटी, नरेन्द्र बहादुर (Bogati, Narendra Bahadur). 2013 (VS 2070). डोटेली भाषाको अध्ययन [Doteli bhashako adhyayan, 'A study of the Doteli language']. MA thesis, Department of Nepali Language Education, Tribhuvan University, Kirtipur. 75 pp. + appendix. https://elibrary.tucl.edu.np/handle/20.500.14540/14339
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 4.1 'डोटेली भाषामा उच्चारण व्यवस्था' (pp. 28-35) treats only vowel, diphthong and consonant pronunciation (tables 1-3) and processes such as assimilation, deaspiration, vowel epenthesis/deletion; section 2.3.4 lists 30-odd morphological/phonological 'features'. No mention of stress, accent, बलाघात, स्वराघात, अनुतान or syllable prominence anywhere (searched the whole text layer after Preeti-to-Unicode conversion).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. IX part IV: Pahari languages and Gujuri. Calcutta. (Kumauni/Eastern Pahari specimens; Doti area)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Older comparative treatment of the Kumauni-Nepali borderland dialects to which Doteli belongs; dsal.uchicago.edu serves page images (JavaScript BookReader, no text), so whether it says anything on accent for the Doti dialect was not checked.

sources.citation: Joshi, B., T. D. Tiwari, A. S. Negi, K. N. Biyogi, H. P. Khatiwada, B. Badu & H. P. Joshi. 2022. Dotyali multilingual dictionary. Mahakali Sahitya Sangam.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent lexicographic work on Dotyali (cited by Bhatt 2023); a front-matter pronunciation guide could give stress conventions.

sources.citation: Bhatta. 2021. Adjacent Consonants and the Universality of Sonority Sequencing Principle in Dotyali Dialects: Syllable Contact Analysis. Jadila 1(3).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: The only phonology-proper article on Dotyali located anywhere (CrossRef); a syllable-structure study is the most likely place for a remark on syllable prominence/stress. Journal site is dead; try author (Tribhuvan/Far Western University) or ResearchGate.

sources.citation: Eichentopf, Stephanie R. 2014. A Sociolinguistic Study of Dotyali. Kathmandu: LinSuN / SIL International (SIL Electronic Survey Report), 161 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy online, not downloaded; the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: Glottolog's main reference; contains transcribed wordlists for several Dotyali varieties that might mark stress, and is the source Wikipedia and Ethnologue rely on. Blocked by an automated-access block here; opens in a normal browser.

sources.citation: Sapkota, Suren. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Dotyali, Achhami, Baitadeli and Darchuleli. Kathmandu: LinSuN, Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 132 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Second Glottolog-listed survey with wordlists; low probability of a stress statement but it is the other primary LinSuN document on the language.

sources.citation: जोशी, खगराज (Joshi, Khagaraj). 2057 VS [2000/01]. डोटेली भाषिका र नेपाली भाषाका व्याकरणिक कोटिको तुलनात्मक अध्ययन. Unpublished MA thesis, Tribhuvan University, Kirtipur.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Earliest Doteli-specific TU thesis; Bogati 2013 says it also treats 'morphophonemic and pronunciation' differences from Nepali; may contain a suprasegmental note. Print only at TU Central Library.

sources.citation: जोशी, खगराज (Joshi, Khagaraj). 2057 VS (2000/01). डोटेली भाषिका र नेपाली भाषाका व्याकरणिक कोटिको तुलनात्मक अध्ययन [Comparative study of the grammatical categories of the Doteli dialect and Nepali]. Unpublished MA thesis, Nepali Language Education, Tribhuvan University, Kirtipur. (cited in Bogati 2013: 8, 74)
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Bogati (2013: 8) summarises it as covering tense, aspect and voice plus 'morphophonemic and pronunciation differences'; not in TU eLibrary (author-name searches return nothing).
